title: Oscar and the Ember
premise: Silas Nakamura, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent seven years selling harmless charms in Vellamark, a city where magic is outlawed and oath-breakers are burned. When a scholar named Wren Corvane shows him a century-old prophecy naming tonight's date, Silas dismisses it—until the city's Ember Ward ignites and drags him bodily into the covenant realm beneath the moon. There he learns the old pact between human and emberkin was broken by his own order, and that restoring it will cost the life of someone he has come to love. Over thirteen turns of the moon, Silas gathers the scattered shards of the covenant, confronts the corrupt magistrate who engineered the ban to hoard magic for himself, and ultimately reforges the oath by surrendering his own swordspeech—not dying, but giving up the power that defined him—so that magic can belong to everyone or no one.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about oaths, debts, and the families people build when their bloodlines fail them.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the night market of Vellamark, Silas sells a luck-knot to a frightened dockworker, hiding the deeper magic that still lives in his scarred hands. Establishes his loneliness, his guilt over the fallen order, and the constant fear of the Wardens. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren Corvane, a disgraced archive scholar, bursts into Silas's stall with a prophecy book that names this exact date—and Silas's true name. Silas wants to burn it; Wren refuses to leave. Their prickly first alliance forms. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity cracking open isolation.

chapters.title: When the Ward Ignites
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At moonrise, the Ember Ward flares blue-white and the street dissolves; Silas and Wren fall through into the Undermoon, the covenant realm, landing in an ash orchard where trees burn without being consumed. Emotional beat: awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Orchard of Small Fires
chapters.summary: They meet Bramblewick, a childlike emberkin spirit who remembers the old covenant and grieves its breaking. She reveals the thirteen-turn deadline: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, both realms seal forever. Emotional beat: grief met with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Order Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Silas's POV, seven years earlier: the Night of Severance, when Magistrate Aldous Vey tricked the swordspeakers into shattering the covenant, then slaughtered them. Silas survived by fleeing. Emotional beat: shame finally given a shape and a name.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, One Road
chapters.summary: Bramblewick gives them the first shard's location: inside the drowned chapel of Saint Ovelun, back in Vellamark but reachable only through a moon-door that opens at low tide. Wren and Silas negotiate terms of trust. Emotional beat: wary partnership becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The pair dives at slack tide, evading Wardens who patrol the harbor, and retrieves the First Shard—but Silas's swordspeech flares visibly, and a Warden sees him use it. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Lantern Streets
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A chase across rooftops and canal bridges as Wardens close in. Wren takes a crossbow bolt meant for Silas, and Silas breaks his own rule by healing her with forbidden speech. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—love now carries a warrant.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: They shelter with Odile, a retired smuggler who once fed runaway swordspeakers, in a safehouse whose walls hold echoes of the dead order. Odile recognizes Silas and forces him to say aloud what he ran from. Emotional beat: confession as the beginning of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Vey's Bargain
chapters.summary: Magistrate Vey's POV. We learn he has been feeding on siphoned covenant magic for years, aging slowly while the city starves of wonder. He offers Silas amnesty and power in exchange for the shards. Emotional beat: seduction of corruption, and how reasonable evil sounds.

chapters.title: The Second Shard Sings
chapters.summary: In the bell tower of Vellamark's cathedral, hidden inside a cracked bell, the Second Shard resonates with Silas's voice—he must sing the old oath-verse he swore never to speak again. Wren transcribes it, preserving what he cannot bear to keep. Emotional beat: reclaiming identity through pain.

chapters.title: Turn Seven: The Moon Turns Its Face
chapters.summary: Halfway point. A quiet interlude at Odile's: Wren and Silas almost speak their feelings; Bramblewick appears in a mirror to warn that the Undermoon is dying faster than expected. Emotional beat: stolen peace before the storm, deepening found-family bonds.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tide Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's apprentice sells their location to Vey. Ambush at the tide gate; Odile dies holding the line so the others escape through the moon-door with the Second Shard. Emotional beat: devastating loss, and rage kindled into resolve.

chapters.title: Undermoon, Dimming
chapters.summary: Back in the ash orchard, they find the emberkin fading—Bramblewick translucent at the edges. The Third Shard lies in the Hollow Court, seat of the emberkin's dead queen, guarded by a thing made of broken oaths. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened by mourning.

chapters.title: The Court of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Silas faces the Oath-Wight, which wears the faces of his dead order and accuses him in their voices. He cannot fight it with a sword; he defeats it by answering honestly—admitting he fled, that he chose survival. It releases the Third Shard. Emotional beat: truth as weapon and absolution.

chapters.title: The Queen's Last Word
chapters.summary: In the Hollow Court's throne room, the emberkin queen's final memory reveals the covenant's true terms: it was never meant to be held by one order—it requires a mortal willing to give up their gift entirely. Silas understands what reforging will cost him. Emotional beat: dawning sacrifice, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She confesses she translated the prophecy months ago and sought Silas deliberately, hoping to save her own brother, whom Vey holds captive. Silas's fury and forgiveness collide. Emotional beat: betrayal within love, and choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: Storming the Spire
chapters.summary: On the twelfth turn, the trio assaults Vey's spire where he is binding the last shard into himself. Wren frees her brother; Bramblewick burns a path; Silas duels Vey, whose stolen magic makes him monstrous. Emotional beat: courage against overwhelming corruption.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Vey, defeated but not destroyed, hurls himself into the moon-door to seize the covenant at its source. Silas follows, leaving Wren to hold the door open from the mortal side. Emotional beat: separation, trust, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: Oath Reforged
chapters.summary: Climax part two. At the covenant's heart, Silas speaks the full oath-verse and surrenders his swordspeech entirely—the gift that made him who he was—pouring it into the covenant so magic flows freely between realms instead of pooling in one man. Vey, denied sole ownership, unravels. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled, not as death but as transformation.

chapters.title: Morning With Ordinary Hands
chapters.summary: Resolution. Silas wakes in the ash orchard, powerless; the emberkin bloom back to life around him, Bramblewick solid and laughing. He returns through the moon-door to find Vellamark's Ward dissolved and small wonders returning to ordinary streets. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Months later, Silas runs a new market stall—selling nothing magical, just honest goods—while Wren reopens the archives to teach covenant history openly. Bramblewick visits through a kitchen mirror. The family they built holds. Emotional beat: home found, not inherited but made.
